metrics.name: Stale window, hardcoded list (until end of run)
Uncached lookup estimate (measured CPU + assumed round trip)

conclusion: A hardcoded list kept sending traffic to dead instances for all 40 s after the crash (8000 failed requests), while a registry stopped it after 12.5 s with a 10 s TTL (2035 failures) and 4.8 s with a 2 s TTL (623 failures), and the faster configuration (2 s TTL with heartbeats every 0.5 s instead of 2.5 s) paid for that with 5x the heartbeat traffic.
setup: 500 in-process instances, 50 killed at 20 s, 20 callers at 100 req/s each, 60 s virtual run in 10 ms ticks, caller cache 3 s, TTL 10 s with 2.5 s heartbeat vs TTL 2 s with 0.5 s heartbeat (+/-10% jitter), same caller start positions and cache phases in all setups, registry round trip assumed as 0.25 ms + exp(mean 0.5 ms) and scheduled on the virtual clock (a refresh lands on the first tick at or after it), no retries, seed 20
